preconditions.expression: 1 <= int(n) <= 1000 and isinstance(n, str) and n.isdigit()
preconditions.description: The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000) representing the depth of the initial complete binary tree.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(q, str) and q.isdigit() and 1 <= int(q) <= 10**5
preconditions.description: The first line also contains an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 10^5) representing the number of queries.

preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in ['1 1', '1 2', '1 3', '1 4', '2'] for line in stdin_lines[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the next q lines is a query of the form '1 x' (where x is 1, 2, 3, or 4) or '2'.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '2' or (line.strip().startswith('1') and int(line.strip().split()[1]) in [1, 2, 3, 4]), for line in stdin_lines[1:])
postconditions.description: Every query line is either a valid operation ('1 x' with x in {1, 2, 3, 4}) or a count request ('2').

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.strip().isdigit() and 0 <= int(output_line.strip()) <= 10**9 for output_line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: For each query of type '2', the output is a non-negative integer representing the number of edges modulo 1000000007.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout_lines) == sum(1 for line in stdin_lines[1:] if line.strip() == '2')
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of '2' queries in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(output_line.strip()) % 1000000007 < 1000000007 for output_line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is a valid modulo 1000000007 result.
